title: Research
text:
My research focuses on developing computational tools and pipelines for multi-omics data integration in cancer biology and translational medicine. I work at the intersection of bioinformatics, machine learning, and clinical research.






Multi-omics Integration & Cancer Biomarker Discovery Oncology Data Analytics Program · IDIBELL


Large-scale analysis of genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and metagenomic datasets to identify genotype–phenotype associations and cancer-related biomarkers.
Key projects:

Gut microbiome profiling in the Catalan population (GCATmb) — characterising microbiome diversity and its associations with health, disease and lifestyle
Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) modelling — multi-cancer constellation model for cancer risk prediction using GWAS and 1000 Genomes/TOPMed reference panels
Colorectal cancer epigenomics — GWAS interaction analyses of environmental exposures (trihalomethanes) and cancer risk
Metabolomics integration — combining metabolomic and genetic data to identify colorectal neoplasia biomarkers

Methods: Nextflow pipelines · SLURM HPC · PLINK · GATK · Bismark · Random Forest · LASSO · Bayesian models · PCA · SVM
WGSRNA-seqWGBSMicrobiomeGWASPRSMachine Learning








Transcriptional Mechanisms in Breast Cancer Progression Molecular and Translational Oncology Group · IDIBAPS


Investigation of molecular mechanisms driving the transition from ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) to invasive breast cancer, combining experimental and computational approaches.
Key findings:

Identified the SEMA3F-NRP1/NRP2 axis as a key factor in the acquisition of invasive traits in breast cancer (Breast Cancer Research, 2024)
Characterised the role of glucocorticoids in promoting DCIS-to-invasive transition via myoepithelial cell apoptosis (Breast Cancer Research, 2018)
Developed complete RNA-seq pipelines from raw FASTQ: QC, alignment (Bowtie2), quantification, normalisation, differential expression (DESeq2/edgeR), and functional enrichment (GSEA)

Methods: RNA-seq · RT-qPCR · Immunofluorescence · Cell culture · RNA/DNA extraction · Bioinformatics pipeline development in R
RNA-seqBreast CancerEpigenomicsRBioinformaticsDCIS








Visiting Researcher — Laboratory of Mina J. Bissell Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory · Berkeley, California


Six-month research stay in the internationally renowned laboratory of Dr. Mina Bissell, pioneer in the study of tissue microenvironment and cancer.

Gained expertise in 3D cell culture and genetic editing techniques
Studied tissue architecture and microenvironmental influences on cellular behaviour
Developed practical skills in advanced cell culture and targeted genetic manipulations

Benvinguda/Welcome!

Hi, I’m Núria, a bioinformatician based in Barcelona with a passion for making sense of large-scale genomic data.
I work at IDIBELL as part of the Oncology Data Analytics Program (ODAP), where I develop reproducible computational pipelines and apply machine learning to uncover cancer biomarkers. My research spans the full multi-omics spectrum, from whole-genome sequencing and RNA-seq to DNA methylation and microbiome data.
Currently, I’m particularly excited about two projects: mapping the gut microbiome of the Catalan population and building polygenic risk score models for multi-cancer prediction. Learn more in publications.
Curious about my work or just want to say hello? Send me a message!!

title: Núria Moragas, PhD
text:
Núria Moragas

Bioinformatics Scientist · NGS · Multi-omics Data Science


PhD-trained bioinformatician with extensive experience in NGS data analysis, epigenomics, and multi-omics integration for translational biomedical research. I develop reproducible and automated pipelines in R and Python to process large-scale genomic and epigenetic datasets, with a focus on biomarker discovery and machine learning for cancer research.
Currently at IDIBELL (Oncology Data Analytics Program), Barcelona. Learn more about me →

About me


Biologist turned bioinformatician, passionate about turning complex genomic data into meaningful biological insights.
I build reproducible pipelines in R and Python for large-scale NGS data — from WGS and RNA-seq to DNA methylation and microbiome — and apply machine learning to discover cancer biomarkers. I work in high-performance computing environments and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams of clinicians, researchers, and data scientists.


Bioinformatics Data Scientist ∙ IDIBELL, ODAP ∙ 2022–Present

Prior to joining IDIBELL, I spent five years at IDIBAPS investigating transcriptional mechanisms in breast cancer progression, developing RNA-seq pipelines and integrating experimental and computational data to identify regulatory biomarkers. My background combines wet lab expertise with advanced computational skills.
